name: PA-13
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 23 points, among the reddest seats in Pennsylvania
Joyce holds a massive financial edge: $3.6 million on hand versus Farnham's $27,000
Prediction markets price Joyce at roughly 98 percent to win
No public polling and no outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's 23-point Republican lean, Joyce's incumbency, and an overwhelming money advantage leave almost no plausible path for Farnham, and prediction markets agree at 98 percent Republican. With no polls or independent spending suggesting competition, the race sits safely in the Republican column.
model.watch: Any late scandal, a surge of outside spending against Joyce, or a major shift in the national environment would be needed to put this on the board.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 13th District covers south-central Pennsylvania and leans Republican by more than twenty points, making it one of the strongest GOP seats in the state. Republican John Joyce has held it since 2019 and is running for another term. No public polls track the race, and outside forecasters largely pass over it as safely Republican.

Democrat Beth Farnham confronts steep odds. She has raised about $101,000 and reports roughly $27,000 on hand, while Joyce has raised $2.7 million and holds about $3.6 million in cash. No outside groups have spent against Joyce. Prediction markets give him roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. Barring extraordinary developments, the district's fundamentals point to his reelection by a wide margin.
